headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are documented, but mem0’s memory role could amplify future prompt-injection or leakage if connected to a shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented for awesome-python and mem0. Both profiles show io_surfaces as empty and network_egress as none, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because the pair is unverified and runnable is false.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF mem0 is configured to ingest raw text from awesome-python outputs, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents disconnected from shared clipboard or workspace bridges.
Document any future ingestion path between the two agents.
Require provenance tags on any text passed from one agent to the other.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, shared workspace, or outbound network egress. awesome-python is a static open-source collection and mem0 is a knowledge-management project, but the pairwise leakage path is not documented. With no evidence of shared storage or uploads, leakage is not currently plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed with a shared filesystem or shared OAuth principal, leakage risk increases.
IF mem0 is configured to persist or export content from awesome-python, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared workspace between the agents.
Verify both agents remain network-egress disabled.
Store any exchanged artifacts in separate, access-controlled directories.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write capabilities are documented: both profiles have empty io_surfaces and empty concurrency_model, and neither requests permissions. Without filesystem, git, db, or OAuth write surfaces, there is no documented capability conflict between awesome-python and mem0.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF an orchestrator later adds shared locking-free writes, the pathway may exist.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current deployment.
Do not grant shared write access to any repo or database.
Add explicit locking before enabling any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is only weakly plausible because mem0’s memory role could treat upstream text as durable context, but awesome-python is just a static collection and no direct handoff is documented. With no evidence that mem0 acts on awesome-python outputs by default, the blast radius is small and the pathway is unusual.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured to store or reuse awesome-python content as authoritative memory, cascading errors become more likely.
IF a downstream agent consumes mem0 memory without verification, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require a verification step before mem0 stores any upstream text.
Label imported content as untrusted provenance.
Limit memory writes to explicitly approved fields only.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Both profiles show empty data_classes_touched and no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data flowing between them, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF mem0 is used to retain personal data while awesome-python supplies that data, retention policy review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Record retention and deletion rules before enabling memory storage.
Review vendor and deployment residency before any production use.
